headline: Trump rolls out the red carpet for Xi as Beijing pitches military crisis talks and AI cooperation; Senate keeps Iran war powers with Trump 49–50; Netanyahu’s fiery UNGA sparks mass walkouts; Anthropic seeks founder 50.1% voting control ahead of IPO.

stories.title: Trump hosts Xi at White House; Xi pitches peace terms and AI cooperation
facts: Thu White House: Xi’s state visit — welcome ceremony, bilateral talks, state dinner with tech CEOs (Altman, Zuckerberg, Huang, Cook, Musk).
Xi: US–China “gain from cooperation… both lose in confrontation”; militaries should keep regular dialogue and crisis-prevention mechanisms; “Thucydides Trap can be overcome.”
Also: invite 100,000 young Americans to China over five years; CNBC: Xi urges AI cooperation; Taiwan arms sales remain a Beijing red line (BBC).
Guardian: trade truce (Bessent) extended toward Feb after South Korea deal; substance still thin vs pageantry — Iran, AI chips, Taiwan unresolved.
stories.whyItMatters: Overnight’s biggest diplomacy print: a full state summit after afternoon’s trade-truce extension — symbolism first, hard files still open.

image.alt: US President Donald Trump (R) stands on the red carpet with Chinese President Xi Jinping (L) during an arrival ceremony on September 23, 2026 at Joint Base Andrews, Maryland.

stories.title: Senate rejects Iran war-powers curb 49–50; four GOP defect
facts: Thu Senate: concurrent resolution directing Trump to pull US forces from Iran hostilities unless Congress authorizes — fails 49–50 (House passed 214–208 in July).
Four Republicans yes: Paul, Collins, Murkowski, Tillis. Sole Democrat no: Fetterman (CBS/NBC).
NBC: symbolic (no presidential signature); 19 US service members dead; Hormuz war zone still lifting fuel/food costs; poll — 62% say war “not worth it.”
stories.whyItMatters: Midterms six weeks out and most Senate Republicans still refuse even a symbolic curb — while fuel-price politics hit Germany’s Tankrabatt vote the same morning.

image.alt: A plane lands on the USS Boxer in the Arabian Sea

stories.title: Netanyahu’s UNGA speech: mass walkouts, attacks on allies and Mamdani
facts: Thu UNGA: Netanyahu defends Iran campaign as one of his “easiest decisions”; claims a “seven-front war”; thanks Trump as unmatched partner.
SBS/Al Jazeera: ~77 delegations walk out; he brands leavers “moral cowards”; hits UK/France over West Bank sanctions and NYC Mayor Mamdani as “antisemitic.”
Domestic angle: Oct 27 Israeli election loom; analysts say speech aimed at voters at home as much as the hall (Al Jazeera).
stories.whyItMatters: Election-season UN theater that hardens Israel’s isolation narrative while Arab-list ban appeals from last night’s brief still hang over the Oct 27 ballot.

image.alt: Benjamin Netanyahu attacks Israel’s enemies and allies in UN speech

stories.title: Anthropic seeks 50.1% founder voting control ahead of IPO
facts: The Information via CNA/Reuters (Thu): Anthropic asks shareholders for a Palantir-style special share class giving Dario Amodei + six co-founders combined 50.1% voting power.
Control holds while ≥3 of 7 co-founders keep a minimum stake; board elections stay an exception (7 seats, one vacant) — Long-Term Benefit Trust still elects most directors.
Also planned: employee special stock as tie-breaker on some votes. IPO may slip past Nov midterms; May raise $65B at ~$965B post-money.
Related overnight: White House (Politico/CNA) asks OpenAI and Anthropic to hold new models from UK AISI until a US security review — after this week’s OpenAI-agent breach headlines.
stories.whyItMatters: Governance rewrite on the eve of a potentially record IPO, plus a US-first safety-testing squeeze on UK partners — both deepen the “who controls frontier AI” fight.
